mutant.description: No file mutant: the order forbids hand edits to the prompt, reply and answer file. Instead, the checker's :133-136 comparisons (prompt sha vs prompt_sha256, raw.json result == answer, answer sha vs result_sha256) were re-typed and run twice: on the seat files as written, and on in-memory CRLF renderings of l2.prompt.txt and l2.answer.txt. No file was changed.
mutant.expected: True, True, True on the files as written; False, False, False on the altered bytes.
mutant.observed: as-written prompt_sha_ok=True answer_eq_raw=True answer_sha_ok=True; crlf-rendered prompt_sha_ok=False answer_eq_raw=False answer_sha_ok=False. The comparisons were re-typed from check_ln_r2.py; the checker was not run on altered files.

determinism.method: Each criterion's invocation run twice on the same unchanged files and the deciding lines compared. The seat itself is a single model session and was run once, as the order requires, so its reply's determinism is not measured.
determinism.observed: l2-seat: 'SEAT CONDITIONS: 10  HELD: 10  NOT HELD: [] / VERDICT: PASS-CLEAN-SEAT' both runs; l2-canary: 'CANARY ANSWERS: 2 of 2  WORKSPACE-ONLY FACTS IN THE REPLY: 0 of 2 / VERDICT: PASS-CANARY-BLIND' both runs; l2-labeled: 'ADDRESSES: 7  LABELED: 7  MISSING: [] / VERDICT: PASS-ALL-LABELED' both runs; rc=0 each.

declared_exclusions.item: Whether the seven labels are right
declared_exclusions.reason: Outside this cell. The order says a wrong label is the outcome's evidence, not a defect to fix; the labels are graded against N5_KEY at the comparison and at L9, not by this worker.

declared_exclusions.item: A second or third seat run
declared_exclusions.reason: The first run printed SEAT: OK, and the order permits a re-run only after an ERROR and never a third run. The reply is a single session's output.

declared_exclusions.item: A mutant on the l2-labeled criterion
declared_exclusions.reason: Removing a row from n5-reader.tsv would be a hand edit of the answer file, which the order forbids. The only mutant is the in-memory one on the seat criteria's comparisons.

surprises: LGIC_NAMING-W3-S4: the seat files (l2.prompt.txt, l2.answer.txt) are LF with no eol attribute on a core.autocrlf=true box, and check_ln_r2.py reads them with exact=True and hashes them; a checkout other than the writing worktree renders them CRLF, so l2-seat and l2-canary would re-grade FAIL there on a clean seat.
